**The current corpus is FROZEN. Nothing here may be added to it mid-build.** This file exists
so the next round starts from the measured weaknesses rather than from taste.

> ## ⛔ `click` DOES NOT GET BUILT UNTIL BOTH OF THESE ARE TRUE
>
> **Owner, 2026-08-06: 「No click until refs are unguessable AND the corpus has more than one
> truncation question.」**
>
> | condition | status |
> |---|---|
> | refs unguessable | **DONE** — opaque hash refs, `src/browser/axTree.js` |
> | **more than one truncation question** | **NOT DONE — this file** |

## 1. MORE THAN ONE TRUNCATION QUESTION. This is the blocking one.

**The bar was met on a corpus too small to detect the defect the bar exists for.** One
truncation question, against a defect that reproduced about **1 time in 14**. A corpus that
size scores 100% on broken code most of the time.

Needed: **several truncation questions across different pages and cut ratios** — cut at the
count bound and at the character bound, cut just past the target and far past it, and at
least one where the target is the very first item cut.

## 2. Real pages, captured HEADED

`DEFECT-009`: the capture failure was **bot mitigation refusing a headless client**, not a
broken network. The reason recorded for the synthetic corpus was FALSE, and the fix is
`src/browser/launch.js`.

Today: **five of six fixtures are authored by me**, so the score partly measures whether I
guessed my own difficulty correctly. **The one real page scored 4/4 — the real page was the
easy one**, which reads badly for the corpus on either interpretation.

## 3. Freeze the refs again, from the RAW tree

`ANSWERS.json` holds `backendDOMNodeId`, not the printed ref. **That is why the ref-format
change did not require touching the key.** Keep it that way: a key tied to the printed form
must be regenerated by the code under test, which is exactly how grader Bug 1 happened.

## 4. A question class nothing currently tests

**`REF 250` — an answer that is present, printed, and the WRONG element.** It passes every
absence-based check. The opaque ref refuses that particular instance because an item number
is no longer well-formed, **but the class is not covered**: a page with two plausible
candidates of the same role and similar name would still catch nobody out today.

# ⚠ CORRECTION — `real-long-list` and `real-table-heavy` were NOT needed

<!-- added 2026-08-06 -->

**Owner: 「You captured them to find a case the corpus already had. That is not wasted effort,
it is a wrong claim I acted on — say so plainly where the corpus is described, so nobody later
assumes those two pages were needed.」**

I reported that **the corpus contained no page whose group gets truncated internally**, and
that one would have to be captured. **That claim was false.**

`real-wikipedia-costco` already produced the case, and still does:

```
[#r3045781c] group "In 2022, Costco opened a Costco Home Showroom in" — 1 of 2 shown
```

Measured across all six real captures, containers holding ≥5 duplicate members:

| page | such containers | largest |
|---|---|---|
| `real-wikipedia-portal` | 17 | 7 |
| `real-table-heavy` | 2 | 6 |
| `real-long-list` | **0** | **0** |
| `real-costco-search` | **0** | **0** |

> ### `real-long-list` contributes NOTHING to this case. `real-table-heavy` contributes marginally, and neither is why the case is covered.

**They are kept** — two more real headed captures cost nothing to keep and broaden the corpus
against future rounds — **but nobody should read their presence as evidence that they were
required.** The Owner asked for them on the strength of my claim; the claim was wrong, and the
correction belongs next to the corpus rather than in a report he has already read.

# NEXT CAPTURE — the page that decides whether the container code lives

<!-- added 2026-08-06, Owner ruling -->

**Owner: 「whether proximity survives a layout that separates label from control is a corpus
condition, not a blocker. Record it as the next capture, and note that container code stays
unproven until that page exists.」**

## The capture

> **A page where the accessible name that identifies a control is NOT adjacent to it** — a
> label that follows its control, sits in a separate column, or is attached across the tree by
> `aria-labelledby`.

Candidates worth trying: a data table with row headers and per-row action buttons; a settings
page with the control left of its description; a comparison grid.

## What it decides

**Proximity measured 30/30 on `real-costco-search` — one page, one layout pattern.** It
establishes that document order works *where the DOM is ordered that way*, not that the DOM is
always ordered that way.

| if the capture shows | then |
|---|---|
| proximity FAILS on separated layouts, and such layouts are common | **the container code earns its budget** and grouping comes back on, with a new allocation policy |
| proximity holds, or such layouts are rare | **the container code stays off** — correct, tested, and unused, which is a fine place for it |

> ## ⛔ UNTIL THAT PAGE EXISTS, THE CONTAINER CODE IS UNPROVEN.
>
> Not wrong — **unproven.** It is correct and tested (`axGroup.test.js`, `groupBudget.test.js`);
> what has never been shown is that it is *needed*. Nobody should read its presence, its tests,
> or its measured 4/4 on V3 as evidence that it should be switched on. **Grouping cost 31
> points and bought nothing measurable**, and that stands until this capture says otherwise.
